title: Inverse powers of occurring normal-subgroup characters
statement: Let $k$ be an algebraically closed field [def-weil-field, def-weil-algebraic-closure], $G$ an affine group scheme [def-sc-group-scheme, def-pc-scheme] of finite type over $k$ [def-weil-finite-type-morphism], and $N\subseteq G$ a closed normal subgroup scheme [def-sc-group-scheme-subgroup]. A finite-dimensional rational representation of $G$ means a homomorphism $G\to\mathrm{GL}(V)$ for a finite-dimensional $k$-vector space $V$ [def-weil-finite-dimensional-subspace], with $\mathrm{GL}(V)$ identified, after a basis choice, with [def-sc-general-linear-group]. A character $\chi:N\to\mathbf G_m$ [def-sc-gm-ga] occurs in such a representation if there is a nonzero subspace $U\subseteq V$ such that, for every commutative $k$-algebra $A$, every $n\in N(A)$ acts on $U\otimes_k A$ by scalar multiplication by $\chi_A(n)$. For every occurring character $\chi$, there exist an integer $m>0$, a finite-dimensional rational representation $W$ of $G$, and a nonzero subspace $T\subseteq W$ such that $n$ acts on $T\otimes_k A$ by $\chi_A(n)^{-m}$ for every $A$ and $n\in N(A)$. This includes nonreduced $G$ and $N$ in positive characteristic. Here $\mathrm{GL}(V)(A)$ means the $A$-linear automorphisms of $V\otimes_k A$; if $V=0$, this is the trivial group scheme $\operatorname{Spec}k$.

source.place: Lemma 5.16, printed pp.102--103: the negative multiple of an occurring character, including the Frobenius reduction for nonreduced groups. Multiplicative notation chi^(-m) replaces additive -m chi.

proof.text: First establish the assertion for smooth $G$, with exponent $m=1$. Choose a line $L\subseteq U$, so that $N$ acts on $L$ through $\chi$. Let $S\subseteq V$ be the sum of all $N$-stable lines. For $g\in G(k)$ and an $N$-stable line $D$, normality implies that $gD$ is again an $N$-stable line: over every $k$-algebra $A$, $n(gd)=g((g^{-1}ng)d)$ and $g^{-1}ng\in N(A)$. Thus $gS=S$, using also $g^{-1}$. The rational-point subspace test, with its smoothness and algebraically closed field hypotheses now satisfied, shows that $S$ is stable under $G$ on every test algebra; hence the restriction is a rational $G$-representation. Notice that $N$ need not be smooth.

source.place: Lemma 5.16, printed p.102, dense rational-points case; Corollary 4.5.

proof.text: Apply character-eigenspace independence to the restriction to $N$. Each $N$-stable line has a scalar action, hence a character: its action is the restriction morphism into $\operatorname{GL}_1$. Therefore $S$ is the direct sum of its finitely many nonzero character eigenspaces. Choose a vector-space complement to $L$ inside the $\chi$-eigenspace and add all the other character eigenspaces, obtaining $S=L\oplus C$ with $C$ $N$-stable on every algebra. This complement is $N$-stable because the action on the entire $\chi$-eigenspace is scalar. In the dual rational $G$-representation $S^*$, the line $\operatorname{Ann}(C)$ is nonzero and has character $\chi^{-1}$ on $N$: for $f$ vanishing on $C$, $(n f)(v)=f(n^{-1}v)$, and on $L$ this is $\chi_A(n)^{-1}f(v)$. The dual action is rational since its matrices are inverse transposes, regular functions on the general linear group. This proves the smooth case, including disconnected $G$ and nonreduced $N$.

source.place: Lemma 5.16, printed p.102, direct-summand and dual argument; Theorem 4.25 in place of Proposition 4.17 for sums of character lines.

proof.text: If $\operatorname{char}k=0$, the affine-group smoothness input makes $G$ smooth, so the preceding two steps finish. Otherwise write $\operatorname{char}k=p>0$ and choose $r\geq1$ and $G\xrightarrow{u}I\hookrightarrow G^{(q)}$, $q=p^r$, from the smooth-Frobenius-image input. Thus $I$ is smooth, affine and of finite type over the same algebraically closed field. It remains to construct an occurring character for a normal subgroup of $I$ whose pullback along $N\to I$ is $\chi^q$.

source.place: Lemma 5.16, printed pp.102--103, Frobenius reduction; Theorem 3.23 and Remark 3.30.

proof.text: Base change $N\hookrightarrow G$, $\rho:G\to\operatorname{GL}(V)$, the line $L$, and $\chi$ along $a\mapsto a^q$. Write their twists as $N^{(q)}\hookrightarrow G^{(q)}$, $\rho^{(q)}$ on $V^{(q)}$, $L^{(q)}$, and $\chi^{(q)}$. Set $H=I\times_{G^{(q)}}N^{(q)}$. It is a closed normal subgroup of $I$: its algebra points are exactly the inverse image of the normal subgroup $N^{(q)}(A)$ under $I(A)\to G^{(q)}(A)$. The normality equations for $N$ remain true after base change. Restrict $\rho^{(q)}$ to $I$ and $\chi^{(q)}$ to $H$, denoting the latter character by $\psi$. The nonzero line $L^{(q)}$ is $H$-scalar of character $\psi$. Indeed, in a basis starting with $L$, the first column of the representation on $N$ is $(\chi,0,\ldots,0)$, and tensoring its coordinate identities with $k$ gives exactly the same column with $\chi^{(q)}$. Relative Frobenius is natural, so $u|_N$ factors through $H$ and $\psi\circ u|_N=\chi^q$. Concretely the coordinate map $b\otimes c\mapsto cb^q$ sends the character coordinate $\chi^*(t)\otimes1$ to $(\chi^*(t))^q$. These are coordinate-ring identities, hence hold for all test algebras, including nonreduced ones.

source.place: Lemma 5.16, printed pp.102--103, Frobenius naturality; explicit twist formulation of the reduction, using the coordinate formula of Remark 3.30.

proof.text: Apply the smooth case already proved in steps 1--2 to the pair $(I,H)$ and its occurring character $\psi$. It gives a finite-dimensional rational representation $B$ of $I$ and a nonzero line $T\subseteq B$ with $H$-character $\psi^{-1}$. Pull this representation back along $u:G\to I$. For every $k$-algebra $A$ and $n\in N(A)$, its action on $T\otimes_k A$ is the scalar $\psi_A(u_A(n))^{-1}=\chi_A(n)^{-q}$. Take $W$ to be this pulled-back representation and $m=q>0$. Pullback changes only the action, so $T$ remains nonzero. This gives precisely the required occurrence.

source.place: Lemma 5.16, printed p.103, inflation from the smooth Frobenius image and dual line.

proof_origin.place: Lemma 5.16, printed pp.102--103; smooth-case argument follows Milne; Frobenius reduction expressed through the base-changed representation and H=I intersect N^(q), avoiding the tensor-power kernel-invariance claim.
